title: Normalized module evaluation compares scalar-extension adjoints
statement: Let F:C→D be a continuous functor between sites J,K, let A,B be ring sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and φ:A→F_*B their structural map. Suppose t:F(c)≅d, e:A(c)≅B(d), and e is exactly φ_c followed by restriction along t inverse. Suppose E:Mod(A)→Mod(B) is left adjoint to module pushforward along φ. For any ring R and map a:R→A(c), let FS and FV be any left adjoints to evaluation at c and d followed by scalar restriction along a and e∘a respectively. Then FS⋙E≅FV. Terminality of c,d is not needed for this abstract statement.

source.place: Tags 03D1--03D3; sectionwise module pushforward, and HRS following diagram (4.4)

proof.text: For each B-module M, the map M(t inverse) identifies evaluation of φ-pushforward at c with evaluation at d. Its semilinearity and the normalization of e show it is R-linear. The inverse map is M(t). Their inverse equations are the presheaf functor equations, and naturality follows from naturality of module morphisms.

proof.text: These evaluation maps give an isomorphism of the composite right adjoint pushforward⋙evaluation_c⋙restrict_a with evaluation_d⋙restrict_(e∘a). Compose the FS adjunction with the E adjunction, transport its right side across this isomorphism, and apply Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq against the FV adjunction.

mathlib_searches.query: An isomorphism of terminal objects under a continuous functor of ringed sites identifies extension of scalars left adjoints using the induced isomorphism on global rings.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No match for the normalized evaluation comparison. Use the sectionwise semilinear maps and uniqueness of adjoints.

mathlib_searches.query: A continuous site functor preserving a terminal object and a normalized ring map identifies left adjoints to scalar-restricted module evaluation
mathlib_searches.verdict: No full comparison theorem. The proof can be written from the underlying module-presheaf maps.
This requires an equivalence of the entire underlying site categories and specified inverse ring maps. The component functor is only a sheaf equivalence, so it does not directly apply.

theorem module_terminal_scalar_comparison
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.IsContinuous J K]
    (A : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (B : Sheaf K RingCat.{u})
    (φ : A ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj B)
    (c : C) (d : D) (t : F.obj c ≅ d)
    (e : A.obj.obj (op c) ≅ B.obj.obj (op d))
    (he : e.hom = φ.hom.app (op c) ≫ B.obj.map t.inv.op)
    (E : SheafOfModules.{v} A ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} B)
    (adj : E ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward φ)
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] (a : R →+* A.obj.obj (op c))
    (FS : ModuleCat.{v} R ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} A)
    (FV : ModuleCat.{v} R ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} B)
    (aS : FS ⊣ SheafOfModules.evaluation A (op c) ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars a)
    (aV : FV ⊣ SheafOfModules.evaluation B (op d) ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars (e.hom.hom.comp a)) :
    Nonempty (FS ⋙ E ≅ FV)
